semantics.AT_REVISION: matches only the named Git commit snapshot
semantics.AFTER_REVISION: matches descendants of the named Git commit and excludes the named commit

revisionDispositionPolicy.currentDisposition: An item's top-level disposition is authoritative for the current working revision; revisionDispositions records the approved boundary-specific history.

reanchoring.reason: The migration branch was rebased after the boundaries were first recorded, which orphaned the original commits: they remained reachable as objects but were no longer ancestors of any branch, so the AT_REVISION and AFTER_REVISION selectors could not be evaluated.
reanchoring.verification: Each replacement was confirmed by comparing the Git blob hash of the governed path at the original and replacement commits; both pairs were byte-identical.
reanchoring.gate: governance.test.js reconciles every original reuse-boundary revision and governed path with the immutable Phase 19A project and boundary lineage records, then asserts that every reconstructed Hadden-Industries/owlapi result commit remains an ancestor of the canonical package HEAD whenever complete Git history is available.

semantics.PRESENT: The governed path belongs to the current repository inventory unless a more specific record says otherwise.
semantics.DELETED: The path was physically removed after replacement acceptance; its provenance and revision-bounded dispositions remain historical audit evidence. A grouped historical selector must enumerate the exact retired paths in artifactPaths.

compatibilityResearch.productionUse: No implementation text, grammar actions, generated parser structure, or control flow was copied; independently authored production behavior is defined by the W3C specification and project-owned tests.

compatibilityResearch.publicBasis: W3C OWL 2 Mapping to RDF Graphs reverse mapping, W3C OWL 2 entity declaration and typing rules, and public OWLRDFConsumer API documentation

compatibilityResearch.question: Whether OWL2VOWL creates a VOWL entity for a property that is declared but carries no property axioms
compatibilityResearch.publicBasis: VOWL 2.0 specification and the pinned OWL2VOWL 0.3.7 reference outputs under src/owl2vowl/test/fixtures/java-reference-outputs/
compatibilityResearch.reason: A corpus difference showed 95 declaration-only properties emitted by VOWLBuilder and absent from the reference output. The output alone could not distinguish between several candidate causes, so the converter's orchestration was read to establish how its entity set is formed.
compatibilityResearch.finding: Entities are established in preParsing by an OWLOntologyWalker driving an EntityCreationVisitor across the whole imports closure, before any axiom-driven phase runs. The later per-property axiom loops decorate entities that already exist; they do not create them. A declared property therefore does appear, which the phase5-structural reference output confirms for a property carrying nothing but a declaration.
compatibilityResearch.productionUse: None. A filter written on the mistaken reading that axioms create entities was reverted in full before any commit, together with the test that encoded it. No implementation text or control flow was copied.

compatibilityResearch.question: What the VOWL-JSON `instances` count on a class actually counts, given that it disagrees with the length of the same entry's `individuals` array
compatibilityResearch.publicBasis: VOWL 2.0 specification and the pinned OWL2VOWL 0.3.7 reference outputs under src/owl2vowl/test/fixtures/java-reference-outputs/
compatibilityResearch.reason: The reference outputs establish that the two fields are independent - only 6 of 9102 class entries carry a non-zero `instances`, and `time-gregorian.ttl` renders `MonthOfYear` with `instances: 1` beside eleven `individuals` - but they cannot reveal the rule that separates them. VOWL 2.0 does not specify the serialisation, so neither source of evidence could settle it.
compatibilityResearch.finding: `IndividualsVisitor` branches on whether the individual's IRI is also present in the class map. When it is, the IRI is recorded as an instance; otherwise it is recorded as an individual. `instances` therefore counts class-and-individual punning, which OWL 2 permits, and never the ordinary members of a class. That is why it is almost always zero and why it is unrelated to the length of `individuals`.
compatibilityResearch.productionUse: None. No implementation text or control flow was copied; the rule was reimplemented independently in VOWLBuilder against project-owned tests.

compatibilityResearch.question: Whether OWL2VOWL restricts entities drawn from imported ontologies to those the importing document references
compatibilityResearch.publicBasis: VOWL 2.0 specification and the pinned OWL2VOWL 0.3.7 reference outputs
compatibilityResearch.reason: tagont.owl produced 77 more properties than the reference output, all of them from imported namespaces rather than declared in the document.
compatibilityResearch.finding: No such restriction exists. The reference output emits 20 skos/core entities that tagont.owl never mentions and 99 such entities for dcat3.rdf, so imports were resolved and imported entities were not filtered by reference. The difference is instead an asymmetry of inputs: tagont.owl imports the long-dead http://www.mindswap.org/2003/owl/foaf, which the reference run could not fetch, while the project's ONTOLOGY_CATALOG maps that IRI to a local FOAF copy. The two sides converted different ontologies.
compatibilityResearch.productionUse: None. The finding is a property of the differential harness rather than of either engine, and no production behavior was changed.

compatibilityResearch.question: Which concrete lexical aliases and document productions belong to OWLAPI 5.5.1's non-standardized DL Syntax dialect when public API documentation and black-box whole-document probes do not expose the grammar
compatibilityResearch.publicBasis: W3C OWL 2 structural class-expression and axiom semantics, public OWLAPI DLSyntaxOWLParser/factory/format documentation, and pinned black-box parser probes
compatibilityResearch.reason: After public documentation and black-box probes established the identity and broad behavior but could not enumerate a concrete compatibility grammar, inspection was restricted to this one grammar file to inventory accepted aliases and productions. Production Java classes, semantic implementation code, and the retained legacy JavaScript parser were not used as implementation specifications.
compatibilityResearch.finding: The public document entry point has observable inconsistencies beyond its grammar inventory: trailing line endings can fail, attached leading colons can be tokenized as identifiers, object-property assertions can be dispatched as class assertions, inverse-property equivalence and numeric data-one-of expressions can become unreachable through document dispatch, and one renderer-shaped unmatched subclass pattern can be silently dropped. The Java differential fixture therefore uses only the whole-document subset the public entry point accepts. The JS parser preserves the inventoried productions, accepts ordinary trailing whitespace and attached or separated property-axiom colons, constructs assertions and numeric data restrictions directly, and retains unmatched subclass axioms instead of dropping them.
compatibilityResearch.productionUse: No implementation text, generated-parser structure, grammar actions, or control flow was copied. The JavaScript lexer and recursive-descent parser are independently structured; project-owned unit, resource, detection, cross-format, Java-oracle, import, and WebVOWL tests define their behavior.

compatibilityResearch.question: What exact operand ordering, primitive-role attribute order, reserved-name behavior, and TBox/ABox document ordering does OWLAPI 5.5.1 enforce where public KRSS2 Javadocs leave those boundaries ambiguous
compatibilityResearch.publicBasis: Public OWLAPI KRSSOWLParser and KRSS2OWLParser Javadocs, distinct document-format identities, W3C OWL 2 structural semantics, and pinned black-box KRSS2 probes
compatibilityResearch.reason: Inspection was restricted to the public parser adapter and grammar after Javadocs and a compiled black-box oracle could not resolve exact argument ordering, ordered role attributes, reserved lexical names, or the TBox-before-ABox whole-document constraint.
compatibilityResearch.finding: KRSS2 uses subject-property-object ordering for related assertions, nested compose before the super-property for role inclusions, an ordered and partly mutually exclusive primitive-role attribute sequence, reserved keyword tokens that cannot stand in for bare entity names, the boolean spellings t/nil, and a TBox* then ABox* document structure. The pinned parser also builds malformed Optional[...] bases for bare names in anonymous/named oracle setups, so the Java differential fixture uses absolute IRIs while independent JavaScript tests define stable document-relative bare-name behavior.
compatibilityResearch.productionUse: No implementation text, semantic action code, generated-parser structure, or legacy JavaScript control flow was copied. The JavaScript lexer and recursive-descent parser are independently structured; project-owned grammar, resource, differential, import, and WebVOWL tests define behavior.

compatibilityResearch.question: Which original-KRSS productions and observable semantics belong to OWLAPI 5.5.1 when public metadata does not expose operand boundaries, ABox commitment, cardinality tokenization, name bases, or right-identity behavior
compatibilityResearch.publicBasis: Published KRSS-family grammar material, public OWLAPI KRSSOWLParser/factory/format documentation, W3C OWL 2 structural semantics, and pinned black-box KRSS1 probes
compatibilityResearch.reason: Inspection was restricted to the public adapter and grammar after public documentation could not freeze the finite grammar. Black-box probes then separated declared grammar from observable structural behavior.
compatibilityResearch.finding: The original dialect has a smaller top-level surface than KRSS2, requires primitive concept and role parents, requires cardinality fillers, accepts only alphanumeric Name entities, and accepts right-identity without emitting an axiom. OWLAPI defects make integer cardinalities unreachable, discard all accepted ABox axioms, construct Optional[...] bare-name bases, and expose singleton Boolean objects outside OWL 2 structural invariants. Each preserved behavior or controlled correction is enumerated in krss1-behavioral-oracle.json.
compatibilityResearch.productionUse: No implementation text, generated-parser structure, semantic action code, or legacy JavaScript control flow was copied. The shared JavaScript core and separate dialect policies are independently structured and defined by project-owned grammar, differential, detection, resource, import, and WebVOWL tests.
